status: PROVISIONAL VISUAL AUDIT; full experiential gate INCOMPLETE

rows.name: Bolt
rows.observed: A compact white-purple head and short trail communicate a quick directed shot. The contact is much less memorable than the launch; the staff does not visibly author a distinct flick.
rows.idea: Preserve the fast minimal projectile. Tighten the staff-tip release and give the real contact one clean directional spark rather than a larger explosion.

rows.name: Life
rows.observed: The green-gold cross ring clearly signals healing, but floats around the caster like a buff badge rather than a decisive breath of recovery.
rows.idea: Pull a compact pulse into the body on the actual heal, then let a few warm motes rise. Keep it instant and distinguish it from the sustained Regeneration ring.

rows.name: Regeneration
rows.observed: The sustained yellow-green crosses and ring remain visible, but look very similar to Life. Continuous decoration communicates an active buff more than living repair.
rows.idea: Make a quiet breathing rhythm with sparse leaves gathering inward on recovery. Preserve a low steady aura and avoid repeated full Life bursts.

rows.name: Ice Blast
rows.observed: The cold fan, scattered chips and icy contact read as frost. Large outlined shards and scattered white marks dominate the release without a particularly brittle material transition.
rows.idea: Preserve the fan. Give the advancing shards a crisp edge and make contacts fracture into smaller directional chips, with fewer persistent white marks around the caster.

rows.name: Earth Shield
rows.observed: The triggered eruption has recognizable stone chunks and a convincing outward breakup. The brief protection and its consumption are less explicit than the eruption itself; this fixture triggers the block directly.
rows.idea: Make one protective stone shell assemble, visibly take the incoming hit, then break into the existing eruption. The single charge should look spent afterward.

rows.name: Lightning
rows.observed: A blue warning ring, descending white bolt, bright impact and dark residue form a recognizable strike. The caster stays visually detached and the aftermath is mostly a ring/scorch rather than branching charge.
rows.idea: Build the staff gather/slam connection, then let a few ground arcs spread from the actual strike and die away. Preserve the strong bolt; do not add new damage or casting delay by implication.

rows.name: Meteor Shower
rows.observed: Separate hot arrivals, bright contacts and cooling patches give this a strong repeated-impact identity. The fire has weight and color; the coarse dark residue is less convincing than the arrivals.
rows.idea: Keep the stagger and repeated impacts. Refine descending trails and crater cooling so each arrival becomes hot debris and spent ground without synchronizing the shower.

rows.name: Ember Spear
rows.observed: The long hot lance and persistent fiery route strongly communicate burning penetration. The straight black strip with orange outline looks mechanically drawn compared with the lively flames above it.
rows.idea: Preserve heat, reach and force. Break up the strip into an irregular scorched path with moving low flame, keeping the spear head distinct from its damaging wake.

rows.name: Infestation
rows.observed: Green black-outlined blobs travel and collect around enemies. They suggest poison, but host infection and transmission look like similar loose particles rather than a sickness taking hold.
rows.idea: Anchor a compact crawling/pulsing growth to the infected host, then let a visibly released spore travel to the next host. Give application and spread different motion.

rows.name: Cinder Field
rows.observed: Orange fire over dark ground convincingly occupies an area. A hard circular border and repeated tall flames read more as a generic fire patch than a bed of cinders.
rows.idea: Keep the heat and saturated color. Emphasize glowing coal pockets, low licking flame and hot ash stirred at real damage contacts; let the edge cool unevenly.

rows.name: Arcane Orbit
rows.observed: Two large purple-white bodies visibly orbit and touch enemies, but their solid outlined, simply shaded surfaces resemble physical balls more than controlled magical energy.
rows.idea: Keep two clear bodies and their orbit. Let light circulate within each shell and leave a short curved particle wake; concentrate the contact accent on the leading edge.

rows.name: Focus Ray
rows.observed: A clear white-purple beam connects caster and target, tracks and stops. Its uniform striped body and modest endpoint response communicate a line better than sustained pressure.
rows.idea: Keep the clean beam. Add subtle forward flow and a concentrated contact point that responds to real ticks, plus a brief narrowing shutdown rather than extra screen effects.

rows.name: Rune Trap
rows.observed: The glyph circle and triggered burst communicate authored magic. Similar rings in the armed, warning and aftermath phases make the state transition less distinct than it could be.
rows.idea: Keep the runic geometry. Draw the inscription once, wait quietly, then snap its symbols inward during the actual trigger warning before the blast opens outward.

rows.name: Seeker
rows.observed: The painted ghost is a clear centerpiece and turns while pursuing. Close pursuit tends to stack bodies over the victim, with weak separation between gliding, touching and dealing damage.
rows.idea: Preserve the body. Add a genuinely lagging trail and a distinct real-contact contraction/release. Compare deliberate passing attacks only as a separately approved behavior prototype.

rows.name: Fire Walk
rows.observed: A low fiery wake visibly follows the caster path. Small isolated flame clumps and checker-like scorch make the trail feel intermittent rather than a continuous hot wake.
rows.idea: Keep the ground-hugging scale. Connect neighboring flames through short-lived heat and embers, show ignition directly behind each step, and let older patches cool in path order.

rows.name: Cross Blade
rows.observed: At gameplay scale the blade is a thin dark rotating cross accompanied by white flecks. Its body and contacts have too little presence for a substantial spinning cutter, and the stronger return is not visually obvious.
rows.idea: Give the existing blade a solid readable edge and short curved cutting wake without expanding its hitbox. Accent the reversal and actual return contacts; keep the three-phase behavior.

rows.name: Lightning Bolt
rows.observed: Repeated local lightning impacts and expanding rings give a strong electrical payoff. The traveling cause is easily lost among the later bright blasts and dark residue.
rows.idea: Make each projectile contact leave a compact electrical mark that visibly becomes its delayed sky strike. Preserve the cascade while shortening distracting spent-ring emphasis.

rows.name: Life Bolt
rows.observed: A shot is followed by green-gold rings and crosses among enemies and around the wizard. The shared healing motif makes the enemy hit, available recovery and received healing difficult to distinguish.
rows.idea: Use a small planted sprout for available recovery and reserve the inward warm pulse for actual healing. Preserve the offensive projectile; do not make damaging contact look like healing the enemy.

rows.name: Meteor Spear
rows.observed: The burning line followed by separate falling fireballs gives the combination a substantial escalating payoff. Hard trail rectangles and overlapping contact bursts make its causal sequence less elegant than its force.
rows.idea: Keep penetration and staggered follow-up impacts. Mark the pierced contacts briefly, then make each descending meteor visibly answer a mark; refine the same artificial trail edge as Ember Spear.

rows.name: Soul Bloom
rows.observed: The slow-motion wisp comparison reveals an appealing luminous soul traveling toward the wizard. At normal speed, infection particles and arrival flashes dominate; short nearby deliveries do not consistently establish the spirit as the centerpiece. The full-health ghost delivery is especially brief.
rows.idea: Keep the approved spirit body and immediate gameplay delivery. Let a visible emergence and absorption remnant complete independently, and render an actual path-following trail. Do not slow healing or add orbit behavior without a separate decision.

rows.name: Steam Field
rows.observed: Soft blue-white connected vapor has volume and shifting lobes; it is unmistakably different from Cinder Field. It convincingly obscures the occupied area, but local scalding consequences are less tangible than the cloud itself.
rows.idea: Preserve the obscuring cloud and color depth. Give its base a few directional vent streams and let genuine scald contacts briefly disturb the vapor locally; do not replace it with a transparent circle.

rows.name: Prism Ray
rows.observed: A broad central ray fans into many colored beams, strongly communicating a combination spectacle. Similar-strength branches and a busy intersection weaken the sense of one ray being refracted at a deliberate focal point.
rows.idea: Make a bright compact refraction knot at the real split, maintain a confident primary ray and give branches lighter material tails. Keep the rainbow fan rather than sanitizing away the fantasy.

rows.name: Frost Sigil
rows.observed: The cold glyph distinguishes the waiting trap, but its large white detonation and dark checker-like aftermath resemble the generic explosion family more than a cold fracture.
rows.idea: Preserve the forceful trigger. Make frost race along the inscription and burst into brittle fragments; fade into cold rime rather than a burnt-looking patch.

rows.name: Magic Missile
rows.observed: Dense opening frames show a small guided dart, sparse wake and compact contact. It stays subordinate to the fight, as a passive cast should; its endpoint could be a little more tactile.
rows.idea: Keep the current scale and simplicity. Refine the tiny contact accent and evaluate repeated sound fatigue at the real automatic cadence; do not add a charge sequence.

rows.name: Bare Spear
rows.observed: A narrow pointed white-purple body establishes a direct thrust and piercing line. The general casting ring is more conspicuous than the spear in some frames.
rows.idea: Keep one sharp point, short wake and local puncture. Reduce competing generic cast decoration before adding anything to the projectile.

rows.name: Bare Slash
rows.observed: A short white-purple filled sector appears at the caster. It conveys affected direction but reads more as a flashing wedge than an edge carving through space.
rows.idea: Keep the quick cone. Concentrate light at an advancing curved edge and taper the tail, with clipped contact particles; do not reintroduce the rejected painted treatment.

rows.name: Bare Nova
rows.observed: An expanding bright rim and sparse runes communicate outward force with a clear ending. The generic cast ring overlaps its identity and weakens the sense of one meaningful front.
rows.idea: Let the damaging front own the release, with a compact central compression and localized edge contacts. Keep the inside quiet after the wave passes.

rows.name: Bare Field
rows.observed: A dark purple disk filled with bright moving glyphs clearly marks active magic, but resembles a decorated bubble more than a low persistent influence on the ground.
rows.idea: Preserve the compact rune field. Ground the glyphs and let real ticks produce a restrained outward pulse instead of constant equally bright decoration.

rows.name: Bare Orbit
rows.observed: Small white-purple moving bodies and curved wakes make the orbit legible with less bulk than Arcane Orbit. Contacts are light and the pattern does not demand the whole screen.
rows.idea: Keep this restrained scale and readable orbit. Give actual contacts a tiny leading-edge spark and retire each wake naturally when its body expires.

rows.name: Bare Trap
rows.observed: A quiet broken ring waits, then becomes a compact runic burst. It is serviceable but the arming and waiting distinction is subtle, and nearby cast-circle decoration competes with the trap.
rows.idea: Use one short closing inscription to signal armed, a quiet waiting state, and one snap on trigger. Empty expiry should erase it without a blast.

rows.name: Atomic
rows.observed: The effect clears enemies after expanding gold lines and a screen tint, but the thin rectangular frame and pale overlay feel like a screen treatment rather than an overwhelming magical release. The fixture directly triggers the blast, not its earning/input flow.
rows.idea: Give the release one strong central collapse-and-expansion and a coherent dissipating shock front. Preserve a brief readable recovery; build exceptional weight through contrast instead of a longer opaque flash.
